analysis:
This batch changes only the CI threat-review tooling under .github/scripts/threat_review. It does not touch provider, coordinator or native code, so no provider asset, boundary or threat (A-001..A-017, TB-002..TB-011, T-041 and others) is directly affected.

bedrock.py (head 46-83): adds a BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY setting. The default 'fixed' keeps the bounded 1-100 allowance. 'workload' starts with limit=0, and plan_calls raises it to planned+1, capped at a bounded ceiling of 100 or less. Exceeding the ceiling sets workload_stopped and raises BudgetStopped. The stopped property (87) includes workload_stopped, so later calls are blocked. The per-call limit check at line 121 is unchanged. These changes are fail-closed. OpenRouter fallback (97-109) still relies on PaidCalls dollar limits; that behavior predates this PR.

budget_scan.py: plan_calls runs before the source, depth and integration stages (head 303-305, 317-327, 332, 367). It plans every source batch even when a cached result is reused, which is conservative. A finished flag is set after the run (400) and included in the snapshot (112).

budget_runner.py:
- Head 175-177 rejects GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT values other than 1 inside the try block. That path records an error and makes no provider call.
- Head 225 marks finished on lifecycle errors.
- Head 38-48 adds a human-review banner when the scan is finished or errored but incomplete, plus a plain 'Scan completed' line.
- The 'complete' predicate (26-29) is unchanged and still requires no errors, full coverage and no pending depth.
- The deep-review permission check (186-190) is unchanged; only its comment changed.

No clearance loosening or new attack surface was identified. The merge-clearance consumer of the result file, the workflow YAML (for example whether attempt-based rerun blocking interacts with required checks) and the PaidCalls limits were not supplied. Integration may want to confirm that workflows set BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY consistently and that the clearance gate reads complete/finished correctly.
